coverage_gaps: No comparison between dense, sparsified, and quantized transformer variants.
Missing discussion of models with ≤10 B parameters beyond TinyLlama (e.g., Phi‑2, MobileBERT‑LLM).
Absence of performance metrics such as latency, perplexity, or downstream task scores for the architectures considered.
Techniques like weight pruning, mixture‑of‑experts, and detailed quantization (4‑bit, binary) are not addressed.
Impact of architecture choices on memory usage and on‑device latency is not quantified.

s2.issue: The claim that the released model files are stored in 32‑bit floating‑point (F32) format is not supported by the provided excerpt.
The statement that the repository provides at least one quantized variant of TinyLlama is not backed by the excerpt.
The observation that the Hugging Face inference pipeline demonstrates loading TinyLlama in half‑precision (torch.float16) is not mentioned in the source text.
The reported 585 downloads in the most recent month lacks supporting evidence in the excerpt.

retry_evidence_summary.answer: The retry stage now fires when the budget allows (1 of 2 runs), but in that run it did not improve any section (0 improved, 3 unchanged, 0 worse, n=3 sections, n=1 run). Whether a retry can help when the fetches succeed is not measured.

report_checks_summary.citation_forms_found: small-language-models: 11 citations, all in the single form [n] ([1] x3, [2] x8); carbon-capture: no citations (no report). The range/multi forms ([5, 6], [5][6], [5-7]) were NOT exercised by either saved report; they are covered only by the parser's own logic, not by this evaluation's data.
report_checks_summary.leak_check_scope: searched each saved file for URLs outside the numbered Sources list, ids (org_/req_/key_), exception names (*Error/*Exception), provider terms (groq, billing, TPD/TPM, 429, service tier) and bracketed non-numeric tokens: zero hits in both reports. The first evaluation's small-language-models report had a raw RateLimitError string with an organisation id and billing URL plus three bracketed internal tokens; the leak is not present in the new reports. Caveat: the sanitiser was exercised by 1 report with plain 'time limit reached / model output unusable' reasons and 1 with 'rate limited' reasons only.

spot_checks.method: fetched the two source pages again with a plain HTTP GET on 2026-10-30 (after the run) and searched the text. The trace does not store page text, so this checks the live page, not necessarily what the worker saw (the trace records only observation_chars: 1901 for the TinyLlama page fetch).

checks.claim: [1] TinyLlama-1.1B has ~1.1 billion parameters and uses the same architecture and tokenizer as Llama 2, enabling drop-in use in Llama-based projects
checks.result: supported by the page text ('exactly the same architecture and tokenizer as Llama 2 ... plugged and played in many open-source projects'; '1.1B parameters')

checks.claim: [1] The model was pretrained on a 3 trillion-token corpus, training commencing 2023-09-01 using 16 A100-40 GB GPUs
checks.result: partly supported: the date and the 16 A100-40G GPUs are on the page, but the page says the project 'aims to pretrain' on 3 trillion tokens, and describes this chat model as fine-tuned from an intermediate 503B-token checkpoint. 'Was pretrained on a 3 trillion-token corpus' is stronger than the page for this model.

checks.claim: [2] MediaPipe LLM Inference API supports Gemma, Phi 2, Falcon and Stable LM; AICore (Android 14) offers LoRA adapters and safety filters; the API is experimental/research-only on Android

spot_checks.omitted_claims_vs_live_page: The 4 claims the critic marked unsupported (and the writer left out): F32 weights, a quantized variant, torch.float16 loading, 585 downloads last month. On the live page: the F32 parameter count (1100052480), torch_dtype=torch.float16 in the code sample, and 'Downloads last month 585' are all present; a 'Browse Quantizations' link is present but the exact '1 model' count was not checked. So at least 3 of the 4 omitted claims are on the live page. Whether they were inside the excerpt the critic saw is not measured. This means the unsupported-claim filter removed claims that the live page supports (a false-positive rate that cannot be quantified from n=4 and one page).

smoke_comparison.caveat: n=1 per system per topic. The second R2 evaluation ran after code changes made in response to the first (run step limit 36 -> 60, retry gate, sanitiser, unverified-claim filter); R1 used step limit 36 and stop fraction 0.8. R0 small-language-models figures come from its second attempt (the first attempt failed with a provider error and was recorded separately). The R2 second-evaluation carbon-capture run was cut short by the Groq daily token limit, so it does not measure the pipeline. No means, no significance.
